nodes.label: A Home Is One JSON Document
nodes.rationale: The 3D scene, the panel and the editor are all built from the document, so swapping the file swaps the home; it stays plain, stable and easy to generate or version.

nodes.label: Metre Coordinate System (x east, z south)
nodes.rationale: Everything is metres seen from above with x growing right (east) and z downwards (south), heights in metres above the floor and angles in degrees, so a plan reads like a drawing.

nodes.label: Rooms as Axis-Aligned Rectangles
nodes.rationale: Rectangles keep wall generation, snapping and opening placement tractable; an L-shaped room is made of two rooms, and where two touch an inner wall appears on its own.

nodes.label: Openings (door, window, open)
nodes.rationale: A gap in a wall given by two end points that must be horizontal or vertical; sill and head place a window, and an 'open' opening is a doorway or missing piece of wall.

nodes.label: Furniture Catalogue
nodes.rationale: Furniture is decoration only, with a fixed type list (sofa, bed, kitchen, plant and so on) plus per-type options such as width, colour and stools.

nodes.label: Lights Schema
nodes.rationale: Six light types (ceiling, pendant, spots, floor, table, strip) with optional y, rot and length overrides; capabilities brightness/temp/colour are omitted for a plain smart plug that only switches.

nodes.label: Air Conditioners Schema
nodes.rationale: An AC hangs on a named wall at a default height of 2.2 m, with a 16–30 °C default target range and an optional thermometer for the room.

nodes.label: Scenes with '*' Wildcard
nodes.rationale: In both the lights and acs maps the key '*' applies to every device and a device's own entry overrides it, which keeps whole-home scenes short; a device the scene says nothing about is left out, so capturing never makes a scene reach further.

nodes.label: Light Groups Schema
nodes.rationale: A named set of lamps switched as one, with ids in the same space as rooms, lights and ACs so a group of the living room's lamps wants living_dining rather than living.

nodes.label: Device link / sensor / tuya Objects
nodes.rationale: A light or AC becomes real when linked to a platform device; Smart Life keeps its own tuya object (deviceId, sensorId, optional codes.switch for a second gang) because its identifiers and data points differ. Device IDs identify hardware, so the link, sensor and tuya objects must be removed before sharing a plan.

nodes.label: Plan Validation Errors
nodes.rationale: A plan that does not add up is never rendered half-way: the panel says what is wrong and where, and the editor shows the same in its status bar.

nodes.label: Camera-Facing Walls Cut Away
nodes.rationale: Walls facing the camera are cut away and inner walls are drawn to interiorWallHeight, so the model stays readable from any azimuth; the azimuth therefore decides which side is open.
